newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares close higher on foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares close higher on foreign buying.

text.p: Shares on the Delhi Stock Exchange closed sharply higher on Tuesday on the back of a late buying spree by foreign institutional investors (FIIs), brokers said.
The bourse's benchmark index closed 13.32 points higher at 837.05.
Brokers said short-covering by speculators also aided the recovery in share prices.

"In view of the budgetary proposal to hike FII investment limit from 24 percent to 30 percent, the foreign investors increased their stakes in companies with strong fundamentals," said Harjit Singh of brokers Wadhwa and Associates.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Friday hiked the investment limit in firms for FIIs to 30 percent from 24 percent in the budget for the 1997/98 fiscal year starting on April 1.
Traders said a sustained rise in share prices also attracted small investors to the market.

"With the revival of buoyancy on the capital market small investors, who were on the sidelines for a long time, also started making selected purchases, which further boosted the market," said another broker.
Reliance Industries rose 7.40 rupees to 314.85 on domestic and foreign institutional buying, brokers said.
ACC surged 73.90 rupees to 1,786 on heavy buying by investors and Bombay based speculators.
State Bank of India gained 7.90 rupees at 334.
ITC jumped 24.15 rupees, to 459.50 on buying by FIIs.
